concepts.title: Rakesh and the Cherry Seed
concepts.section: The Cherry Tree, Let us read I
concepts.definition: Six-year-old Rakesh presses a cherry seed into a shady corner of his grandfather's Mussoorie garden and almost forgets it; the seed's quiet rise into a tree teaches him that luck grows only when it is put to use.
concepts.key_idea: Grandfather's line that nothing is lucky if you put it away turns a discarded seed into a living lesson.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr104.txt, The Cherry Tree, Let us read I

solution_steps.explain: Retell the main happenings in one or two sentences.

Say the message of the text in one sentence of your own.

concepts.title: The Cherry Tree's Struggles and Survival
concepts.section: The Cherry Tree, Let us read II
concepts.definition: The young tree survives a goat that eats its leaves, a grass-cutter's scythe that cuts it in two, and heavy snow; each time it sends out new shoots, until it blossoms pink and bears sour cherries that the birds love.
concepts.key_idea: Cherry trees are tough, as grandfather says; the tree's will to live answers every blow with fresh growth.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr104.txt, The Cherry Tree, Let us read II

solution_steps.explain: Note each injury the tree suffers, season by season.
Describe the new leaves and shoots that follow each blow.
Recall the blossoms, the fruit and the visitors the grown tree earns.

concepts.title: Grandfather's Company: Bond across Generations
concepts.section: The Cherry Tree, Let us read
concepts.definition: Grandfather and Rakesh share stories by the charcoal fire, newspapers read aloud, and the garden; growing side by side with the tree, the boy learns patience while the old man finds shade and joy under its leaves.
concepts.key_idea: The tree binds the two ages: planted by a child, enjoyed by the old, it measures how both have grown.
concepts.textbook_ref: hepr104.txt, The Cherry Tree, Let us read

solution_steps.explain: List the moments the two spend together through the seasons.
Note how their talk keeps returning to the growing tree.
Say what the tree finally means to each of them.

concepts.title: Word Meanings: Stunted, Tang and Foliage
concepts.section: The Cherry Tree, Let us learn
concepts.definition: Hill-country words are fixed by context: stunted means stopped from growing to usual size, tang is a strong sharp taste, foliage means green leaves, and the outskirts are the edges of a town.
concepts.key_idea: Nature words like haunches, scythe and blossoms place the reader in the Himalayan garden.

worked_examples.question_pattern: What advice did Grandfather give about the lucky cherry seed?

solution_template.explain: Rakesh asks whether cherry seeds are lucky and wants to keep the seed.
Grandfather says nothing is lucky if you put it away; luck must be put to use, so the seed is planted.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How did the cherry tree respond after the scythe cut it in two?

solution_template.explain: A woman cutting grass sweeps her scythe and the tree is cut in two.

solution_template.action: note the reply of the tree
solution_template.explain: By the next summer it has sent out several new shoots with tender green leaves, refusing to die.
